parakeet: Here's the conflict in a single sentence. God is in control, then either God's plan keeps changing, or God is allowing people to live in contradiction to it on a massive scale. Both options undermine the idea of a sovereign, benevolent, all-knowing deity. Either God can't stop moral chaos, which means he's not omnipotent, or God didn't foresee the fallout, which means he's not omniscient, or God doesn't care enough to intervene, which means he's not benevolent. If we were in a theocratic simulation governed by a perfect being, we wouldn't be fighting wars over which version of God is right. We'd all be living in the same code.
